attribution: A body of scriptures regarded by followers as revealed by Shiva; many authors over centuries
period: The oldest surviving Shaiva scriptures are generally placed from about the 5th–7th centuries CE onward, with many later works
summary: The corpus of Shaiva scriptures that governs initiation, worship, temple construction, yoga and theology, especially for Shaiva Siddhanta.
whyRead: The Agamas shaped temple religion in South India and the ritual and theological life of Shaivism. They show Tantra as a full religious system of doctrine, ritual and contemplation.
questions: How do ritual, knowledge and meditation fit together?
What is initiation, and why does it matter?

keyTeachings.title: Four subjects
keyTeachings.text: Agamas are traditionally organised around four subjects (padas): knowledge (vidya or jnana), ritual (kriya), yoga and conduct (charya).

keyTeachings.title: Initiation (diksha)
keyTeachings.text: Initiation by a qualified teacher is central. In Shaiva Siddhanta it is understood as an act of Shiva's grace that removes bonds and qualifies one for worship and liberation.

keyTeachings.title: Temple and image
keyTeachings.text: Many Agamas give detailed rules for temple building, installing images and daily and festival worship, which still govern South Indian temple practice.

keyTeachings.title: Theology of Pati, Pashu, Pasha
keyTeachings.text: The Siddhanta Agamas set out the three eternal realities of Lord, soul and bond, later systematised in Tamil by Meykandar.

structure.label: 28 principal Shaiva Agamas in the Siddhanta tradition
structure.note: Traditionally divided into 10 Shaiva and 18 Raudra Agamas, with many subsidiary texts (upagamas)
